title: Scoutline integration kickoff - proxy & SDK evaluation
summary: Intro/discovery call to map Scoutline's current stack, requirements for SDK/langchain integrations, gateway/proxy pattern, rate-limits/quotas, and observability hooks. Redwood team to follow up with security docs, pilot plan, and sample SDK snippets. Agreed to run small-scale perf benchmark against typical query shapes.
topics: rate limiting, per-route quotas, burst policies
observability hooks (OpenTelemetry, trace-id, token-level cost breakdown)
hosting options: Hosted API vs Dedicated vs Private (VPC / on-prem)
transcript:
[00:00] Meeting header: 2026-04-03 15:00 UTC | Duration: 57m
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Jonah Kim (Redwood SE), Alex Rivera (Scoutline CTO), Priya Shah (Lead ML Eng), Tom Becker (Platform Eng), Nina Lopez (Security)

[00:12] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh quick intro. I'm Maya Patel, account exec for Redwood Inference. Jonah is our solutions engineer who will run through the integration details.
[00:21] Jonah: Hi all, thanks. Quick agenda: understand your flow, talk SDK/connectors, gateway patterns, quotas, and observability.
[00:30] Alex: Great, thanks. We run Scoutline search and document Q&A. Currently have a microservices backend on k8s, we proxy LLM calls through an internal gateway; most traffic is short prompts but a tail of long context recency.
[00:44] Priya: To add, we use LangChain in our orchestration layer and LlamaIndex for retrieval ingestion. We're exploring consolidating calls and moving away from a brittle lambda-based adapter.
[00:55] Jonah: Useful. Do you currently use any vendor SDKs or open API wrappers?
[01:02] Tom: We built a small wrapper around OpenAI SDK; it's thin. We also have a gateway that performs auth and rate-limiting.
[01:10] Maya: Are you evaluating hosted vs dedicated vs private? Which constraints push you one way or the other?
[01:16] Alex: Primary concerns: data residency for EU customers, predictable latency for chat use-cases, and unit cost as we scale. Also security: strict audit logs and KMS.
[01:27] Nina: From security, SOC2a? we need SOC 2 type II reports, SSO (SAML), and HSM-backed keys ideally.
[01:37] Jonah: Redwood has Hosted for fast onboarding, Dedicated for predictable GPU pools, and Private for VPC/on-prem with customer-managed network. We can support SAML and KMS integrations; we'll share specifics.
[01:49] Priya: On the SDK side, how mature are Redwood's SDKs for LangChain/LlamaIndex? We rely heavily on LangChain chains and LlamaIndex indexes.
[01:58] Jonah: We have official SDKs and LangChain connector examples; LlamaIndex examples exist but sometimes require small adapter glue. For retrieval-augmented generation, we recommend using our streaming responses and token-level cost metadata so you can correlate embeddings/calls.
[02:16] Alex: Do you support batched embeddings? We need to push large embedding pipelines during off-peak.
[02:22] Jonah: Yes, batching and async embeddings supported, and Redwood Optimize can suggest quantization or batching profiles. For Dedicated you can reserve capacity for embedding windows.
[02:33] Tom: Gateway pattern question: We currently have a sidecar proxy that enforces per-API-key quotas and shapes bursts. Does Redwood expect a direct SDK call from service, or do you recommend passing through our gateway?
[02:43] Jonah: Both are viable. Many customers do a lightweight gateway for auth and routing and call Redwood's SDK from backend services. Another pattern is a central gateway that forwards requests to Redwood Hosted with a token exchange. Important to pass through trace-id so observability ties back.
[02:59] Priya: How are per-route quotas handled? We want per-customer quotas, plus per-route soft-limits and hard-bucket burst protection.
[03:08] Jonah: Redwood supports token- and request-level quotas. For Hosted we have per-route quotas and rate limits that can be configured; for Dedicated you can enforce capacity reservations and Redwood Console exposes quota dashboards. We also support policy routing that can fall back to cheaper model variants on throttling.
[03:27] Alex: Is there a way to do token-bucket style bursting per-tenant?
[03:32] Jonah: Yes, token-bucket and leaky-bucket semantics are supported through rate-limit profiles. We can sync with your gateway to offload enforcement or have Redwood enforce it at the API layer. There's a small delta in latency depending on where enforcement happens.
[03:47] Tom: Latency: for chat we need p95 < 400ms for short turns; is Dedicated guaranteed?
[03:55] Jonah: Dedicated provides predictable throughput and lower variance; SLAs are available on certain tiers. For p95 400ms depends on model selection and sequence lengths; we recommend smaller quantized models or GPU types tuned for low-latency. We'll run a benchmark with your exact payloads.
[04:12] Priya: Observability: can we get OpenTelemetry traces and per-token cost breakdown surfaced in our datadog/jaeger?
[04:20] Jonah: We emit hooks and you can forward events. Console provides token-level cost and latency breakdown. There's an OpenTelemetry collector plugin and trace-id pass-through is supported. For loghooks we can deliver audit logs to your S3/GCS or send to a SIEM via connectors.
[04:37] Nina: For compliance we need end-to-end encryption at rest and in transit, and key control for private deployment. How does Redwood handle keys in Private mode vs Hosted?
[04:47] Jonah: In Hosted we manage keys but support customer-managed KMS via key wrapping integrations; in Private you control keys in your KMS/HSM. We'll include an architecture note.
[05:02] Alex: Ok, integration specifics: Our LangChain chains use the OpenAI-style API. How much effort to move to Redwood SDK?
[05:10] Jonah: Minimal. Our SDK exposes an OpenAI-compatible surface in most languages; we also have direct LangChain adapters. For LlamaIndex we have example adapters and recommend a small shim to map embeddings + metadata.
[05:25] Priya: Any gotchas with KV cache or long context windows? We use local KV caches for session state.
[05:32] Jonah: Redwood runtime manages KV cache for model-internal state; if you maintain session-level caching you can combine both. Watch for cache invalidation on model rollouts — we provide hooks to flush KV on version switch.
[05:47] Tom: Do you support rate-limited background ingestion? e.g., embeddings pipeline throttled to off-peak, with spike allowance.
[05:54] Jonah: Yes, you can configure burst windows and scheduled jobs. For Dedicated you can reserve capacity for nightly batch windows to avoid impacting peak.
[06:03] Alex: Regarding costs, how transparent is per-route token billing? We need to bill end customers.
[06:09] Maya: Console shows token breakdown per API key/route and you can export usage per tenant. We also provide webhook exports or raw CSVs for billing pipelines.
[06:20] Priya: We'd like to run a pilot: 2-week scale test, LangChain chains pointing at your Hosted first, then test Dedicated if latency is good.
[06:29] Maya: Sounds good. Next steps would be: we send a pilot plan and security pack; you run small benchmark payloads; we'll set up a trial API key and share SDK snippets.
[06:39] Nina: Also need data retention/erasure details for GDPR.
[06:44] Jonah: We'll include retention settings and erasure process in the security doc.
[06:49] Alex: Any competitors we should watch? We're also talking to OpenAI and a couple of infra vendors, and a shop called ModelHostX.
[06:57] Maya: Noted. We'll include comparative notes.
[07:02] Tom: One more technical: can we side-load a custom tokenizer or quantized model in Private?
[07:08] Jonah: In Private deployments there is more flexibility; shipping custom model artifacts needs an ops sync but it's supported for on-prem. We'll outline the process.
[07:18] Priya: Great. Can you also provide a sample LangChain agent config that uses Redwood streaming?
[07:24] Jonah: We'll share a snippet and a repo link.
[07:28] Maya: Ok quick recap and owners.
[07:31] Jonah: Recap: share security pack, pilot plan, SDK snippets, run benchmark with provided payloads, schedule a follow-up in ~1 week.
[07:39] Maya: Thanks everyone, will follow up via email.

[07:47] (call ends)
